Title: My Coffee Truck
My coffee truck still parked by the sea the wind stole the sugar packets nobody cared to retrieve
You two sat under the beach umbrella one sentence, three different faces she said, “I’m fine” you said, “whatever” even the waves rolled their eyes at it
I was just grinding coffee beans not responsible for anyone’s past love is sometimes like an iced Americano bitter for a reason sweet, but never enough
I guess that still counts as love just love with too much going on saying you don’t care while checking who looks back first
I guess that still counts as love no need to make it tragic people aren’t that noble people aren’t that bad
The sunset fell into the paper cups you were still debating who got hurt more she chewed the straw flat you made your apology sound light
I’m not taking either side I’ve just seen too many summers some people wrap their truth too nicely some call it freedom when it’s only fear of staying
I guess that still counts as love just love with too much going on one says, “I’m leaving” then waits to be stopped
I guess that still counts as love no need to settle every score nobody here is the villain you’re just both very good at acting strong
Coffee’s almost ready. Love, I don’t know much about. I only know this: people who really want to leave usually don’t stay for a second cup.
I guess that still counts as love just love a little ridiculous still caring way too much while pretending to stay cool
I guess that still counts as love smile a little, don’t expose it all after the sea breeze passes through aren’t we all about the same?
My coffee truck still parked by the sea you finally stopped talking and I was closing up quietly
